title: Cross-node PP/TP saturation probe and p95 regression detector
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable cross-node benchmarking harness that isolates saturation modes between pipeline-parallel (PP) and tensor-parallel (TP) partitions and adds automated p95 regression detection. The goal is to reproduce long-tail latency/p95 regressions observed in multi-GPU deployments, measure tokens/sec under realistic KV-cache warm/cold conditions, and provide tooling to triage whether bottlenecks are compute-bound, allreduce/collective-bandwidth bound, or interconnect-saturation related.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end harness can spin up 2-8 node PP+TP topologies and run configured workloads deterministically
Prometheus + histograms exported for per-step latencies (token-gen, allreduce, KV read/write) and a derived p95 timeseries for the whole request path
Automated regression detection runs daily and raises an alert when p95 increases more than 10% over a 24h baseline and persists for >3 evaluation batches
Documentation (Confluence) describes how to add a new model, change TP/PP splits, and interpret the p95 signal
Initial experiment run with bert-style and long-context LLM (2k tokens) produces reproducible bottleneck classification report
test_plan: Workloads: short (128 tokens), medium (512), long (2048) with both batched and single-request arrival patterns
KV cache modes: cold-start (no cache), warm-cache (prefill 1k prefixes), prefix-sharing scenario (cache hits across requests)
Topology sweep: TP only (max TP, PP=1), PP only (TP=1), hybrid TPxPP combos (e.g., TP=8/PP=2, TP=2/PP=8)
Microbatching sweep: microbatch {1,2,4,8} combined with effective batch (tokens/sec) target
Network stress: synthetic background allreduce traffic to emulate noisy NICs / NVLink contention
Measurement: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, CUDA kernel times, NCCL allreduce times, PCIe/NVLink counters, GC/host CPU stalls, queue lengths
results_summary: Initial baseline (4-node hybrid, TP=4 PP=2) produced 62k tokens/sec sustained with p95=210ms for 512-token workload
When microbatch=1, p95 increased to 680ms and NCCL allreduce contribution rose from 12% to 46% of end-to-end latency — indicates collective overhead at PP handoff is dominant for small microbatches
Cold KV-cache runs reduced tokens/sec by ~28% and increased p95 variance; recommending cache-prefill for production steady-state or prioritized warm paths for tail-sensitive routes
Interconnect stress test demonstrates NVLink saturation for TP-heavy configs (TP>=8) where per-step allreduce times degrade non-linearly; suggests limiting TP per-node for latency-sensitive customers

Regression detector (EWMA + sliding-window median absolute deviation) triggered on a synthetic noisy run and correctly grouped the anomaly with increased allreduce times; false-positive rate on 7-day window ~4% (needs threshold tuning)
decisions: Ship a first-pass regression detector using EWMA + 24h baseline and 3-sample confirmation before paging
Expose recommended microbatch floor in runtime docs and add a runtime guardrail that warns when configured microbatch < 2 on PP handoffs
Add a small NCCL tuning experiment (adjust algorithm, use hierarchical allreduce) as follow-up before changing model mappings
Make cache-prefill an opt-in pattern in the dedicated/private deployment templates and offer tooling to generate prefill workloads
next_steps: Tune regression detector thresholds and run for 10 days to measure false-positive/negative rates
Create a GitHub PR with harness code and unit tests: PR link attached in artifacts
Add NCCL algorithm sweep to the harness and rerun the TP>=8 topology tests
Coordinate with infra to provision a dedicated NVLink-saturated cluster for controlled experiments
Draft runtime documentation and a runbook for oncall to triage p95 alerts (linked in artifacts)
